headline: Jio's record IPO opens as Trump says India trade deal is pretty close

segments.title: The big picture
segments.script:
Good morning. It's Wednesday, the twenty-first of October, and this is your Market Brief.

Three things matter most today. First, the Jio Platforms share sale opens this morning. At around 30,200 crore rupees, it is the largest initial public offering India has seen.

Second, Washington and New Delhi sound closer than ever on a trade deal. President Trump says it is pretty close, and his Secretary of State, Marco Rubio, is in Mumbai urging India to buy more American energy and defence equipment.

And third, oil is back near 110 dollars a barrel, after a sharp fall in Indian shares in the last session.

segments.title: How markets closed
segments.script:
Let's start with the last session, on Monday. It was a rough one. The Sensex fell nearly 900 points, and the Nifty slipped below 22,900 to close at 22,889. Nearly 5 lakh crore rupees of market value was wiped out in a day. Private banks and IT stocks led the selling, with weak global cues and rising crude adding to the pressure.

Foreign institutional investors sold shares worth around 1,148 crore rupees. Domestic institutions cushioned the fall, buying about 3,200 crore rupees.

This morning looks calmer. GIFT Nifty was trading around 23,031, up nearly 100 points, which points to a positive start. Asian markets are higher too.

Now the levels analysts are watching. Technical analysts quoted by Moneycontrol see 23,000 to 23,200 as the key resistance zone. On the downside, they see support at 22,800 and then 22,500. Milan Vaishnav of Gemstone Equity Research says the rebound can extend as long as the Nifty defends the zone of 22,300 to 22,675.

One more number puts this year in perspective. Edelweiss Mutual Fund research shows Indian shares fell about 6.8 percent in 2026 through September, while US stocks gained nearly 13 percent and gold about 11.6 percent.

segments.title: IPOs and deals
segments.script:
Now to the big event. The Jio Platforms offer opens for subscription today. The price band is 1,065 to 1,119 rupees a share, and the company is selling about 27 crore new shares to raise roughly 30,213 crore rupees. It has already raised about 8,110 crore rupees from 212 anchor investors, including BlackRock, Capital Group, Fidelity and T. Rowe Price.

Reliance shareholders have their own quota of 2,500 crore rupees, and the Economic Times notes that eligible shareholders can apply in both the shareholder and the retail categories. Allotment is due on the twenty-sixth, and listing on the twenty-eighth.

Mint reports that non-bank lenders and brokerages are in a marketing overdrive, offering short-term loans to retail investors. Akash Ambani told Moneycontrol that Jio is entering public markets to build a sustainable business with many growth engines.

More offers are lining up. EAAA India Alternatives opens a 1,200 crore rupee offer on the twenty-sixth, entirely a sale by existing shareholders, with its anchor book on the twenty-third. SFC Environmental Technologies opens on the twenty-seventh, with 150 crore rupees of new shares. And sources tell Moneycontrol that OYO's parent, PRISM, will cut the new-share part of its offer by nearly half, to 3,350 crore rupees, thanks to strong cash generation.

On the deals front, Sun Pharma plans to raise 10,000 crore rupees through rupee bonds, to refinance bridge loans taken for its 11.75 billion dollar Organon acquisition. The first tranche of 7,000 crore rupees carries a coupon of 8.2 percent. And Transrail Lighting is buying 49 percent of NOPL Pace Green Energy, which is building a 990 megawatt solar portfolio in Maharashtra under the PM-KUSUM scheme.

segments.title: Results roundup
segments.script:
To results, starting with lenders. Piramal Finance reported a 67 percent jump in September-quarter profit. Credit costs stayed at 1.1 percent, and net slippages were the lowest in 11 quarters. Nomura named it its top pick among non-bank lenders.

HDFC Bank's net interest margin fell to a 12-quarter low. But Mint points out that core operating profit grew and asset quality improved. Bajaj Finance, IREDA and Yes Bank also reported, with the Economic Times describing the IREDA and Yes Bank numbers as mixed. All three are in focus today, along with L and T Technology Services, Hindustan Zinc and Infosys.

In real estate, DLF bounced back with pre-sales of 3,800 crore rupees, driven by luxury homes in Gurugram. Mint says its full-year target of 20,000 crore rupees still looks like a steep climb.

Coming up, brokerages expect Eternal, the parent of Zomato and Blinkit, to report strong growth with better margins. And Titan's board meets on the fifth of November to approve its numbers.

segments.title: Economy and policy
segments.script:
Now the economy, and first, trade. President Trump says a deal with India is pretty close, and will be very different from earlier pacts. The US ambassador, Sergio Gor, says Washington wants two-way trade above 500 billion dollars within three years, up from a record 240 billion.

Separately, the India and New Zealand free trade agreement came into force on Tuesday. Moneycontrol estimates it could open up a 6 billion dollar export opportunity, with pharma and jewellery among the gainers.

On trade numbers, India's goods trade deficit was 30.2 billion dollars in September. That's narrower than 33 billion dollars a year ago, as exports grew faster than imports.

On tax, net direct tax collections rose 13.2 percent to 13.37 lakh crore rupees up to the fourteenth of October. Securities transaction tax jumped 51 percent, to 46,840 crore rupees.

On the rupee, bankers estimate the Reserve Bank has spent about half of a 140 billion dollar foreign capital haul defending the currency. Foreign exchange reserves stood at 734.6 billion dollars on the second of October, about 51 billion below their September peak. A Moneycontrol analysis of IMF forecasts says the weak rupee pushes India's 5 trillion dollar milestone back a year, to 2029, though India should still overtake Japan and the UK in 2027.

Prices are a worry in places. Retail sugar inflation hit 29.8 percent in September, the highest in the new consumer price series. The drought is squeezing maize supplies, pitting poultry farmers against ethanol makers. Yet in Nashik, tomato prices have crashed 65 percent in a week on a supply glut.

segments.title: Around the world
segments.script:
Around the world, oil is the story. Brent crude rose to about 109.6 dollars a barrel early this morning, on Red Sea shipping risks and threats to Saudi oil sites. It topped 111 dollars on Tuesday. Tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has collapsed, with one dataset counting just four arrivals in the week to the eleventh of October. Traders are weighing conflicting signals on talks to end the US-Iran war, and that has kept gold on the back foot as well.

In Europe, gas prices hit 90 euros for the first time in almost four years before slipping back, and anger over fuel prices is driving protests in France.

On Wall Street, stocks recovered from early losses on strong earnings and softer oil. AI worries resurfaced after a weak South Korean listing, and the chipmaker SK Hynix is down 31 percent this month. But AI shares rallied after hours on strong preliminary sales from Super Micro.

In China, growth beat forecasts, with industrial production up 5.5 percent in September.

segments.title: Stories you're following
segments.script:
An update on the Jio IPO you're following. The offer opens today and closes on Friday, and lenders and brokerages are offering short-term loans to draw in retail investors.

And on the India and US trade deal you're following. A day after Marco Rubio called the deal very, very close, President Trump now says it is pretty close. Rubio also called India a refining superpower, and said the US delegation would discuss producing oil in Venezuela with Reliance.

segments.title: Your money
segments.script:
Finally, your money, starting with tax. Form 141 replaces four forms for tax deducted at source, covering rent, property purchases, contractor payments and crypto transfers, from the first of April 2026 under the new Income Tax Act. The Central Board of Direct Taxes has notified Form 173A for eligible foreign investors claiming tax exemptions on government securities. And interest on the New Development Bank's Maharaja rupee bonds is now exempt from tax deduction at source for eligible investors, from the tax year 2026-27.

Two tribunal rulings are worth noting. The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal upheld a 50 lakh rupee addition against a woman who declared 4.81 lakh rupees of income but bought a 50 lakh rupee LIC policy, because she could not prove the money came from her late husband's family business. And the Ahmedabad bench held that a 1.5 crore rupee payout after a 23-year land dispute is taxable as capital gains, not as income from other sources.

For borrowers, the Reserve Bank's quarter-point hike took the repo rate to 5.5 percent, and several banks have raised their lending rates. Fresh investments into gold fund of funds have been halted, to limit foreign exchange outflows. And central government employees will watch today's Cabinet meeting, which Mint says has raised hopes of a 3 percentage point rise in dearness allowance.

A warning too. Zerodha's Nithin Kamath has cautioned about pump-and-dump schemes run through WhatsApp groups, after the Enforcement Directorate froze accounts worth 200 crore rupees. And the Kerala High Court ordered SBI to refund 3.73 lakh rupees to a retired principal who lost money after sharing an OTP with a fraudster.

One date for your calendar: today is the last day to buy JSW Dulux shares to qualify for its one-for-ten stock split.

That's your brief. Today, watch the first-day subscription numbers for Jio, the Cabinet's decision on dearness allowance, any word on the trade deal from Rubio's visit, and crude near 110 dollars. Have a good day.
